authorities.exact_section: Highlights of Prescribing Information and Product Information — opioid analgesic; CII; label updated June 23, 2026
M.G.L. c.94C, §19B(b)-(c) — separate statewide-standing-order authority for pharmacist dispensing of opioid antagonists

results.Problem: None identified after independent option-by-option verification. Oxycodone is an opioid and Schedule II. Section 18D is current and requires a pharmacist dispensing a Schedule II opioid to inform the patient of the prescription opioid's potential adverse risks and offer to dispense an opioid antagonist. A is false because §18D contains no exception for a patient who already possesses unexpired naloxone. B states the required information-and-offer duty; the statute requires an offer, not acceptance or purchase. C improperly converts the offer into mandatory acceptance as a condition of dispensing. D adds conditions not found in §18D: a separate antagonist order or documented elevated overdose risk from the opioid prescriber. E adds an opioid-naive limitation not found in the statute. Section 19B's standing-order/access authority is a separate pathway and does not erase the §18D duty.
results.Proposed_Explanation: When a pharmacist dispenses oxycodone, a Schedule II opioid, M.G.L. c.94C §18D requires the pharmacist to inform the patient of the prescription opioid's potential adverse risks and offer to dispense an opioid antagonist. The statute does not condition the opioid dispensing on the patient's acceptance or purchase of the antagonist, does not excuse the duty because the patient already has unexpired naloxone, and does not require a separate antagonist order, elevated-risk documentation, or opioid-naive status. Separate §19B naloxone access/standing-order authority should not be conflated with this dispensing-triggered §18D duty.
